request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "Watched due" figure (`watched-due-total`): the due-totals of everyone the signed-in user watches, added up, and 0.00 when they watch no one. All 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

It only needed front-end changes, because the app already stored who watches whom and could return a user's watched people:

- **`features/people/people.ts`**: a new `watchedDueTotal` figure adds up the watched people's due-totals. It uses the same capped amounts as each person's row, so a held person or the sheet's cap is reflected straight away. It's a straight sum, like "My crew due", not the sheet total that leaves out the highest and lowest figures. People whose due-total is n/a are skipped.
- **`features/header/header.ts`**: the new `watchedDueTotal` input and its header entry.

No server, data or audit changes were needed. Watching and unwatching still write their existing `PERSON_WATCHED` and `PERSON_UNWATCHED` records.
